newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian hard-left hopes for privatisation accord.
newsitem.headline: Italian hard-left hopes for privatisation accord.

text.p: The leader of Italy's hard-left said on Friday he hoped for compromise on the privatisation of ENI, Enel and Stet.

"Communist Refoundation will try to find an agreement on the privatisations to prevent a government crisis from happening," Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said during a television interview to be broadcast later on Friday.
"We must avoid a crisis, we have to find a compromise, we are talking about strategic sectors for the country."
Bertinotti's party, which backs the ruling centre-left coalition but remains outside the government, holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament.
Bertinotti hoped 51 percent of telecoms holding Stet could remain under state control. He remained "completely opposed" to the privatisation of electricity utility Enel.

Stet shareholders last week approved a golden share to be held by the Treasury in the future private group, giving the state special voting rights for up to three years after it loses majority control in the sell-off.
The Stet sale is due to take place this autumn after it is merged with its fixed-line telephone operator Telecom Italia.
